q.s: Kot Diji and Amri are typical sites of which phase of the Harappan Civilisation?
q.x: Kot Diji, Amri and Sothi belong to the Early Harappan phase (3300-2600 BCE); the Late phase is marked by OCP and Cemetery-H.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the chronology of the Harappan Civilisation is correct?
o: Kot Diji and Amri are typical sites of the Late Harappan phase.
Bricks in the 1:2:4 ratio belong only to the Late Harappan phase.
Cemetery-H culture belongs to the Early Harappan phase.
John Marshall dated it to 3250-2750 BCE by Mesopotamian cross-dating.
q.x: Marshall used Mesopotamian cross-dating; Kot Diji and Amri are Early Harappan, Cemetery-H is Late Harappan and 1:2:4 bricks are Mature Harappan.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT an export item of Harappan foreign trade?
q.x: Silver and tin were imported by the Harappans; carnelian beads, lapis lazuli and timber are listed as exports.

q.s: Evidence of a terracotta plough model has been found at which Harappan site?
q.x: A terracotta plough model was found at Banawali (Haryana); Allahdino shows well irrigation and Shortughai canal traces.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Evidence of well irrigation comes from Allahdino in Sindh.

q.s: Which of the following southern powers is NOT mentioned in Ashoka's Rock Edicts II and XIII?
q.x: The edicts name the Chola, Pandya, Satiyaputra and Keralaputra; the Satavahanas rose to power only after Ashoka.

q.s: Which of the following was a feature of the Harappans but NOT of the Rigvedic Aryans?
q.x: The Rigvedic Aryans were rural and pastoral; planned cities belonged to the Harappans.

q.s: What was the standard unit of value and exchange in the Rigvedic economy?
q.x: The Rigvedic economy was mainly pastoral and the cow (gau) was the unit of value.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Rigvedic economy is correct?
o: The horse is mentioned fewer times than the cow.
Land was the standard unit of value.
It was mainly pastoral, with agriculture secondary.
Coins were the main medium of exchange.
q.x: The economy was pastoral and the cow was the unit of value; asva occurs about 215 times and gau about 176 times.

q.s: Among the Ikshvakus, the performance of the Ashvamedha conferred which title on the king?
q.x: For the Ikshvakus the Ashvamedha gave the title Swarat, while the Vajapeya gave Samrat.

q.s: Remains of an Ashvamedha altar have been found at:
q.x: An Ashvamedha altar of the Ikshvaku period was found at Nagarjunakonda.

q.s: The Ratnins of the Later Vedic period were honoured in the Ratnahavimshi rite, which formed part of:
q.x: The Ratnahavimshi rite in which the Ratnins were honoured was part of the Rajasuya.

q.s: How many royal functionaries called Ratnins formed the Later Vedic king's council?
q.x: The Ratnins were twelve royal functionaries.

q.s: Who founded the Samkhya school of Indian philosophy?
q.x: Samkhya, regarded as the oldest darshana, was founded by Kapila; Gautama founded Nyaya.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the six orthodox schools is correct?
o: The Vaisheshika school recognises nine dravyas (substances).
q.x: Vaisheshika has nine dravyas; Samkhya (Kapila) pairs with Yoga, and Nyaya (Gautama) with Vaisheshika.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Rigvedic gods is correct?
o: Indra was regarded as the messenger between gods and men.
Agni was given the title Purandara, the fort-breaker.
The first hymn of the Rigveda is addressed to Indra.
Varuna was regarded as the upholder of the cosmic order, rita.
q.x: Varuna upheld rita; Agni was the messenger and receives the first hymn; Indra was Purandara.

q.s: Which Rigvedic god was called Purandara, the fort-breaker?
q.x: Indra, the war god with about 250 hymns, was called Purandara.

q.s: Shravasti was the capital of which Mahajanapada?
q.x: Shravasti was the capital of Kosala.

q.s: The capital of the Vajji confederacy was:
q.x: Vaishali was the seat of the Vajji (Lichchhavi) confederacy.

q.s: Which of the following patrons of Buddhism ruled between Ashoka and Kanishka?
q.x: The order is Ashoka (3rd c. BCE), Menander (2nd c. BCE) and Kanishka (1st-2nd c. CE).

q.s: The Bharhut stupa is located in which state?
q.x: Bharhut is in Satna district of Madhya Pradesh.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Devnimori is near Shamlaji in Aravalli district, Gujarat.

q.s: Who led the Jain monks who stayed back in Magadha and later came to wear white robes?
q.x: Sthulabhadra led the monks who stayed in Magadha (Svetambaras); Bhadrabahu led the group to the south.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a belief of the Digambara sect?
o: Women must be reborn as men to attain moksha
q.x: The Svetambaras say Mahavira married Yashoda; the Digambaras hold he never married.

q.s: Which edict of Ashoka defines Dhamma as 'few faults, many good deeds'?
q.x: Pillar Edict II gives this definition of Dhamma.

q.s: Which Rock Edict of Ashoka records the Kalinga war?
q.x: Rock Edict XIII records the Kalinga war; Rock Edict I bans animal slaughter.

q.s: The Mauryan rock-cut elephant at Dhauli is located near which city?
q.x: The Dhauli elephant is on the Daya river near Bhubaneswar.

q.s: The Kanaganahalli relief slab showing Ashoka belongs to which period?
q.x: The Kanaganahalli slab is a later Satavahana-period relief, not a Mauryan work.

q.s: The Sondani inscription, composed by Vasula, records the victory of:
q.x: Sondani records Yashodharman's victory; the Gwalior inscription records Mihirakula's rule.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Junagadh inscription - Repair of the Sudarshana lake
Eran boar inscription - Toramana's first regnal year
q.x: The Gwalior inscription records the rule of Mihirakula.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Brihat Jataka is by Varahamihira; the mathematician Mahavira wrote Ganitasarasangraha.

q.s: Hastyayurveda, a treatise on the treatment of elephants, is attributed to:
q.x: Hastyayurveda is attributed to Palakapya; Vagbhata wrote Ashtangahridaya.

q.s: Which Rashtrakuta ruler overthrew the Chalukyas of Badami?
q.x: Dantidurga ended Badami Chalukya power in the mid-8th century.

q.s: Which Pallava ruler captured Vatapi in 642 CE and took the title Vatapikonda?
q.x: Narasimhavarman I defeated Pulakesin II and occupied Vatapi for about 13 years.

q.s: The Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta came to India during the reign of:
q.x: Ibn Battuta came in Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign and served as qazi of Delhi.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Muhammad bin Tughlaq is correct?
o: He joined the public celebration of Holi.
He was succeeded by his uncle Firoz.
Ibn Battuta reached India only after his death.
q.x: He celebrated Holi and consorted with Jinaprabha Suri; Firoz was his cousin, and Ghiyasuddin founded the dynasty.

q.s: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was written by:
q.x: Minhaj-us-Siraj wrote the Tabaqat-i-Nasiri in 23 volumes; it was translated by H. G. Raverty.

q.s: Fatawa-i-Jahandari, a work on the political theory of kingship, was written by:
q.x: Barani wrote both the Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and the Fatawa-i-Jahandari.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a work of Amir Khusrau?
q.x: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi was written by Barani (and Afif); the other three are Amir Khusrau's.

q.s: Amir Khusrau's Ashiqa deals with the romance of Khizr Khan and:
q.x: Ashiqa is the romance of Khizr Khan and Deval Rani; Kamala Devi was Deval Rani's mother.

q.s: Under Sher Shah Suri, the state's share of land revenue was fixed at:
q.x: Sher Shah fixed the share at one-third of the average produce.

q.s: Sher Shah's land revenue system served as the model for the bandobast of:
q.x: Todar Mal's Bandobast under Akbar built on Sher Shah's survey-based system.

q.s: Which Mughal ruler wrote his autobiography in Turki?
q.x: Babur wrote the Tuzuk-i-Baburi in Turki; Akbar wrote no autobiography.

q.s: Jahangir wrote his memoirs, the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, in:
q.x: The Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri is in Persian.

q.s: The jagirdari crisis of the Mughal empire developed mainly under:
q.x: Under Aurangzeb there were too many mansabdars for too few jagirs.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Mughal jagirdari crisis is correct?
o: It reduced the pressure of revenue demand on the peasants.
It arose because there were too few mansabdars for the jagirs available.
It arose because there were too many mansabdars for too few jagirs.
q.x: Too many mansabdars chased too few jagirs under Aurangzeb, raising pressure on the peasants.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Mughal war of succession (1657-59) is correct?
o: Deorai was the last battle of the war.
Samugarh was the last battle of the war.
Dharmat was the first battle of the war.
q.x: The order was Bahadurgarh, Dharmat, Samugarh, Khajwa and Deorai (1659).

q.s: In the Mughal army, the term 'Dagh' referred to:
q.x: Dagh was horse branding; Tashiha was the muster check.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Tashiha was the muster check; Dagh was branding.

q.s: Hereditary jagirs of Mughal chiefs in their homelands, which were not transferred, were called:
q.x: Watan jagirs were hereditary; only tankhwah jagirs were transferred every 3-4 years.

q.s: Mansabdars kept waiting without being assigned any jagir were said to be in a state of:
q.x: Waiting without a jagir was called bejagiri.

q.s: In the 17th century Masulipatnam was the chief port of which kingdom?
q.x: Masulipatnam was the Qutb Shahi port for kalamkari and saltpetre.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Cambay - Old Gujarat port that declined with silting
Masulipatnam - Qutb Shahi port of kalamkari
Lahari Bandar - Qutb Shahi port of kalamkari
q.x: Lahari Bandar was the port of Thatta in the Indus delta.

q.s: The Punjabi romance Heer Ranjha was written by:
q.x: Waris Shah wrote Heer Ranjha.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Bhaktmal is by Nabhadas; Keshavdas wrote the Ramchandrika.

q.s: The Bhakti saint Ravidas came from which family background?
q.x: Ravidas was a leather-tanner; Namdev was a tailor, Sena a barber and Dhanna a Jat peasant.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Sena was a barber; Namdev was a tailor.

q.s: Guru Nanak was born in 1469 at:
q.x: Guru Nanak was born at Talwandi; he settled and died at Kartarpur, where the langar began.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Guru Nanak is correct?
o: The Guru ka Langar began at Amritsar.
q.x: Mardana was his companion; he was born at Talwandi, the langar began at Kartarpur and Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa.

q.s: The Chishti saint Baba Farid was the disciple of:
q.x: Baba Farid was the disciple of Bakhtiyar Kaki; Nizamuddin Auliya was Farid's own disciple.

q.s: Verses of which Sufi saint are included in the Guru Granth Sahib?
q.x: Baba Farid's compositions are part of the Guru Granth Sahib.

q.s: By which treaty (1802) did the Peshwa accept the subsidiary alliance of the British?
q.x: The Treaty of Bassein (1802) made Peshwa Baji Rao II a subsidiary ally.

q.s: The Peshwaship was abolished by the British in:
q.x: The Peshwaship ended in 1818 after the Third Anglo-Maratha War.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse?
q.x: Awadh was annexed in 1856 on grounds of misgovernance; Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur came under the Doctrine of Lapse.

q.s: Who was the adopted son of Rani Lakshmibai whose claim the British refused to recognise?
q.x: Damodar Rao was the Rani's adopted son; Nana Saheb was the adopted son of Baji Rao II.

q.s: The first French factory in India was set up in 1668 at:
q.x: The French opened their first factory at Surat in 1668 and at Masulipatnam in 1669.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the French in India is correct?
o: Their Masulipatnam patent was granted by the Mughal emperor.
Their first factory was set up at Surat in 1668.
Chandernagore was their first factory in India.
q.x: Surat (1668) was first; the Masulipatnam patent came from Golconda; the renaming came in 2006.

q.s: Siraj-ud-daula was provoked when the English gave asylum to Krishna Das, the son of:
q.x: Sheltering Krishna Das, son of Raj Ballabh, was among the causes of conflict with Siraj.

q.s: Who commanded the British forces at the Battle of Assaye (1803)?
q.x: Arthur Wellesley, later Duke of Wellington, won at Assaye and Argaon; Lord Lake won at Delhi and Laswari.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Assaye was won by Arthur Wellesley.

q.s: 'Prosperous' British India (1901), a critique of colonial economic policy, was written by:
q.x: William Digby wrote 'Prosperous' British India.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: G. Subramania Iyer - Some Economic Aspects of British Rule in India
M.G. Ranade - Essays on Indian Economics
R.P. Dutt - Some Economic Aspects of British Rule in India
q.x: R.P. Dutt wrote India Today.

q.s: At AITUC's Nagpur session of 1929, the moderates under N.M. Joshi walked out and formed:
q.x: N.M. Joshi's group formed the Indian Trade Union Federation in 1929.

q.s: Who presided over the 3rd and 4th sessions of the AITUC?
q.x: C.R. Das presided over the 3rd and 4th sessions; Lajpat Rai presided over the first.

q.s: Provincial autonomy under the Government of India Act, 1935 came into force on:
q.x: Provincial autonomy began on 1 April 1937.

q.s: Which of the following provinces did NOT have a bicameral legislature under the Government of India Act, 1935?
q.x: The six bicameral provinces were Madras, Bombay, Bengal, UP, Bihar and Assam.

q.s: After the Brahmo Samaj split of 1866, Debendranath Tagore's group came to be known as:
q.x: Debendranath's body became the Adi Brahmo Samaj; Keshab led the Brahmo Samaj of India.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Brahmo Samaj is correct?
o: Keshab founded the Indian Reform Association in 1875.
After 1866 Keshab Chandra Sen led the Brahmo Samaj of India.
After 1866 Debendranath Tagore led the Brahmo Samaj of India.
The Brahmo Marriage Act was passed in 1856.
q.x: Keshab led the Brahmo Samaj of India; the Marriage Act is of 1872 and the Reform Association of 1870.

q.s: The 1917 resolution sought to replace the term 'Panchama' in the Andhra region of Madras Presidency with:
q.x: It proposed 'Adi Andhra' in Madras and 'Adi Hindu' in Hyderabad.

q.s: Who presided over the second Adi-Andhra conference of 1919?
q.x: Chilukuri Venkataswamy presided in 1919; Kusuma Dharmanna urged socialism in 1936.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: First Panchama Mahajana Sabha at Vijayawada - 1917
q.x: The Madras Communal G.O. was first issued in 1921, not 1937.

q.s: The Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924) was founded by:
q.x: Ambedkar founded the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha in 1924.

q.s: Kandukuri Veeresalingam's novel Rajasekhara Charitra is based on:
q.x: Rajasekhara Charitra (1878) is based on Goldsmith's The Vicar of Wakefield; Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu on Gulliver's Travels.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Rajasekhara Charitra - Based on The Vicar of Wakefield
Kasiyatra Charitra - Based on Gulliver's Travels
Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu - Based on Gulliver's Travels
Brahma Vivaham - Satire on the opponents of reform
q.x: Kasiyatra Charitra is Enugula Veeraswamayya's travelogue.

q.s: The All India Women's Conference held its first meeting in 1927 at:
q.x: The AIWC first met at Poona in 1927.

q.s: Who among the following was NOT a founder of the Women's Indian Association (1917)?
q.x: The WIA was founded at Adyar by Besant, Cousins and Jinarajadasa; Ramabai Ranade started the Ladies' Social Conference (1904).

q.s: The Bengali weekly Sambad Kaumudi (1821) was started by:
q.x: Rammohan Roy started Sambad Kaumudi (1821) and the Persian Mirat-ul-Akhbar (1822).

q.s: Somprakash (1858), started on Vidyasagar's plan, was edited by:
q.x: Dwarkanath Vidyabhushan edited Somprakash.

q.s: The Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress (1906) was presided over by:
q.x: Dadabhai Naoroji presided at Calcutta in 1906, where 'Swaraj' was declared the goal.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the four resolutions of the Calcutta Congress of 1906?
o: Annulment of the partition of Bengal
q.x: The four resolutions were Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education.

q.s: Which movement made the Indian National Congress a mass movement for the first time?
q.x: The NCM (1920-22) spread nationalism to the masses; the British made no concession of Swaraj.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Non-Cooperation Movement is correct?
o: It was launched after the Simon Commission's arrival.
The British conceded Swaraj within a year of its launch.
It turned the Congress into a mass movement for the first time.
q.x: The NCM (1920-22) spread nationalism to the masses; no concession of Swaraj followed.

q.s: Which of the following leaders was NOT among the 'Responsivists' who favoured cooperation with the government after 1924?
q.x: Lajpat Rai, Malaviya and Kelkar were Responsivists; Motilal Nehru led the Swarajists, who left the legislatures in 1930.

q.s: The Chirala-Perala movement was led by:
q.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya led Chirala-Perala; Alluri led the Rampa rebellion.

q.s: The Palnadu pullari (grazing tax) movement is associated with:
q.x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu led the Palnadu pullari movement; Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary led the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign.

q.s: Gandhi undertook his first hunger strike in India during the:
q.x: Gandhi fasted for the first time in India in the Ahmedabad mill workers' struggle.

q.s: The Ahmedabad struggle of 1918 led by Gandhi was over:
q.x: The issue was mill wages (the plague bonus); revenue remission was the issue at Kheda.

q.s: Goa was liberated from Portuguese rule in December 1961 through:
q.x: Goa was freed by Operation Vijay; Operation Polo was the Hyderabad action of 1948.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the India-China war of 1962 is correct?
o: China declared a unilateral ceasefire on 21 November 1962.
China declared a unilateral ceasefire on 26 October 1962.
The disputed Chinese road ran through the Tawang tract.
The Dalai Lama fled to India during the war.
q.x: The ceasefire came on 21 November 1962; the road ran through Aksai Chin and the Dalai Lama came in 1959.

q.s: Potti Sriramulu was born on 16 March 1901 at:
q.x: Potti Sriramulu was born in Madras; his ancestral village Gajula Dinne is in Nellore district.

q.s: At which session in 1928 were the Ceded districts renamed 'Rayalaseema'?
q.x: The Nandyal session of 1928, presided over by S. Radhakrishnan, adopted the name Rayalaseema.

q.s: The name 'Rayalaseema' for the Ceded districts was proposed by:
q.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao proposed the name at Nandyal in 1928.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 is correct?
o: It came into force on 1 October 1956.
It made Andhra Pradesh the first linguistic state of independent India.
It created 16 states and 3 Union Territories.
It came into force on 1 November 1956.
q.x: The Act came into force on 1 November 1956 and created 14 states and 6 Union Territories.

q.s: The first linguistic state of independent India was:
q.x: Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953; Andhra Pradesh was the first state formed under the SR Act.

q.s: The Democratic Telugu Desam Party (1984) was formed by:
q.x: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao led the DTDP; Marri Chenna Reddy led the National Democratic Party.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Democratic Telugu Desam Party (1984) - Nadendla Bhaskara Rao
Telugu Desam Party (1982) - N.T. Rama Rao
Swatantra Party in AP (1959) - N.G. Ranga
q.x: The National Democratic Party was led by Marri Chenna Reddy.

q.s: Who is the Governor of Andhra Pradesh in 2026?
q.x: Justice (retd.) S. Abdul Nazeer is the Governor of Andhra Pradesh.

q.s: Who is the Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in 2026?
q.x: K. Pawan Kalyan is the State's only Deputy Chief Minister.

q.s: Which Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 lists institutions such as IIT, NIT, IIM, AIIMS, a railway zone and a steel plant?
q.x: The Thirteenth Schedule lists educational institutions and infrastructure; the Eleventh covers irrigation projects.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT listed in the Thirteenth Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
q.x: The Thirteenth Schedule lists institutions and infrastructure such as IIT, AIIMS, a railway zone and a steel plant; the High Court is covered by separate sections of the Act.

q.s: The oldest evidence of paddy in India, dated to about 6500 BCE, comes from:
q.x: Lahuradeva has yielded the oldest paddy; Koldihwa in the Belan valley was earlier thought to have the oldest rice.

q.s: Lahuradeva, known for early rice cultivation, is in which state?
q.x: Lahuradeva is in Sant Kabir Nagar district, Uttar Pradesh.

q.s: Acharya Nagarjuna's Suhrullekha ('friendly letter') was addressed to which Satavahana king?
q.x: The Suhrullekha was addressed to Yajnasri Satakarni.

q.s: Nagarjuna's Mulamadhyamakakarika is a treatise of which school of Buddhist philosophy?
q.x: Nagarjuna founded the Madhyamika (Sunyavada) school.

q.s: Which of the following museums is NOT located in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: The Salar Jung Museum is in Hyderabad, now in Telangana.

q.s: The Bapu Museum is located at:
q.x: The Bapu Museum (old Victoria Jubilee Museum) is in Vijayawada.

q.s: The Chikkulla plates belong to which Vishnukundin ruler?
q.x: Chikkulla - Vikramendra Varma II; Ramatirtham - Indravarma; Tummalagudem - Govinda Varma I.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Khanapur plates belong to Madhava Varma II.

q.s: The Aihole inscription of Pulakesin II was composed by:
q.x: Ravikirti, Pulakesin II's Jain court poet, wrote the Aihole prasasti in Sanskrit.

q.s: The Aihole inscription is engraved on which temple?
q.x: The inscription is on the Meguti Jain temple at Aihole.

q.s: Rajendra Chalukya, who united the Eastern Chalukya and Chola lines, ruled under the name:
q.x: Rajendra Chalukya became Kulottunga I, the first Chalukya-Chola king.

q.s: Kundavai, daughter of Rajaraja Chola I, was married to which Eastern Chalukya king?
q.x: Kundavai married Vimaladitya; Kulottunga I married Madhurantaki, daughter of Rajendra II.

q.s: The Nayankara system of the Kakatiyas was introduced by:
q.x: The Nayankara system is credited to Prataparudra.

q.s: The Kesari Samudram (Kesamudram) tank was built by the Kakatiya ruler:
q.x: Prola I built the Kesari Samudram tank.

q.s: Rudramadevi took the title 'Rayagajakesari' after her victory over the:
q.x: Rayagajakesari commemorates her victory over the Yadavas of Devagiri.

q.s: Marco Polo visited which Kakatiya port during the reign of Rudramadevi?
q.x: Marco Polo called Motupalli 'Mutfili'.

q.s: Who was the Gaja Sahini (chief of elephants) of the Kakatiya king Ganapatideva?
q.x: Jayapa Senani was Gaja Sahini; Gangaya Sahini was the Ashwa Sahini (cavalry chief).

q.s: In the Kakatiya army, 'Mula Balam' referred to:
q.x: Mula Balam was the king's own standing army, as distinct from Nayankara contingents.

q.s: Srinatha's Haravilasam is dedicated to:
q.x: Haravilasam is dedicated to the merchant Avachi Tippayya Setti; Sringara Naishadham to Mamidi Singana.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a work of Srinatha?
q.x: Amuktamalyada was written by Krishnadevaraya.

q.s: Which Reddi ruler is credited with building forts such as Kondaveedu, Kondapalli and Dharanikota?
q.x: Prolaya Vema, founder of the Reddi kingdom, is credited with 74 forts.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Kondapalli fort is correct?
o: Its main gate is the Golconda Darwaza.
It was built by Kakatiya Ganapatideva.
Its main gate is the Dargah Darwaza.
The palace inside it is the Chowmahalla Palace.
q.x: The main gate is the Dargah Darwaza and the palace is the Tanisha Mahal; the fort is credited to Prolaya Vema.

q.s: The capital of the Gajapatis of Orissa was:
q.x: The Gajapatis ('Lords of Elephants') ruled from Cuttack, c. 1434-1541.

q.s: Malik Ambar was the Abyssinian regent of which Deccan Sultanate?
q.x: Malik Ambar served the Nizam Shahis and resisted Jahangir.

q.s: Khirki, founded by Malik Ambar, later came to be known as:
q.x: Khirki was renamed Aurangabad.

q.s: The founder of the Qutb Shahi dynasty, who was killed by his son Jamsheed, was:
q.x: Sultan Quli built the Golconda Jama Masjid and was murdered by Jamsheed.

q.s: Which Qutb Shahi ruler, who came to the throne in 1550, built the high walls of Golconda fort?
q.x: Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah built Golconda's walls and gained Kondavidu after 1565.

q.s: What was the main source of income of the Qutb Shahi state of Golconda?
q.x: Land revenue, collected through tax farming, was the main source; mines and ports added to it.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Qutb Shahi revenue system is correct?
o: Machilipatnam port was never leased out.
Land revenue was collected through tax farming to the highest bidder.
Port customs were the main source of income.
Diamond mines yielded no income to the state.
q.x: Land revenue, farmed out, was the main source; Machilipatnam was leased for 1,80,000 pagodas.

q.s: Who founded the Tuluva dynasty of Vijayanagara in 1505?
q.x: Vira Narasimha, son of Narasa Nayaka, founded the Tuluva dynasty.

q.s: The rule of the Aravidu dynasty began with Tirumala Deva Raya at:
q.x: After Talikota (1565), Tirumala shifted to Penukonda.

q.s: Chapa Koodu (Dasa Samaj), which promoted inter-caste dining, was started in Palnadu by:
q.x: Brahma Naidu started Chapa Koodu, a sahapankti (common dining) practice.

q.s: Which Chola prince was recalled from Vengi in 1118 to serve as co-regent of his father Kulottunga I?
q.x: Vikrama Chola left the Vengi viceroyalty in 1118 to become co-regent.

q.s: In the Palnadu war, Nayakuralu Nagamma was the minister of:
q.x: Nagamma was Nalagamaraju's minister; Brahmanaidu was Malideva's minister.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kota Bhimaraju II - Backed Nalagamaraju with Rudradeva
q.x: Balachandra was Brahmanaidu's son, killed in the war.

q.s: In 1336 Kapaya Nayaka recovered Orugallu (Warangal) from:
q.x: Kapaya Nayaka, with Ballala III and others, drove out Malik Maqbul in 1336.

q.s: Prolaya Nayaka of the Musunuri family, being childless, was succeeded by his cousin:
q.x: Kapaya Nayaka succeeded Prolaya Nayaka.

q.s: The Vitthala temple at Hampi is dedicated to:
q.x: The Vitthala temple enshrines Vithoba, a form of Vishnu.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Krishna temple - Bala Krishna idol from Udayagiri
q.x: The Vitthala temple enshrines Vithoba; Pampapati is the deity of the Virupaksha temple.

q.s: The Panchaloha cannon is associated with which fort of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Udayagiri fort in Nellore district, built by the Vijayanagara rulers and later taken by Golconda, has the Panchaloha cannon.

q.s: Why was the British judicial system under the Company criticised in Andhra?
o: Its slow and costly procedure increased litigation and debt
It gave too much power to village panchayats
It was conducted only in Telugu
q.x: Replacing village panchayats with slow, costly courts increased litigation and debt.

q.s: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham's prize-winning novel was:
q.x: Ramachandra Vijayam was his prize-winning novel; he also founded the Ram Mohan School (1909).

q.s: 'Maa Telugu Talliki', now the state song of Andhra Pradesh, was written by:
q.x: Sankarambadi Sundarachari wrote 'Maa Telugu Talliki'.

q.s: The Communists formally withdrew the Telangana Armed Struggle in:
q.x: The struggle went on after the Police Action of September 1948 until it was withdrawn in October 1951.

q.s: Praja Natya Mandali (1943) was the Andhra wing of:
q.x: Praja Natya Mandali was the Andhra IPTA; Burrakatha was its main folk form.

q.s: The play 'Maa Bhoomi' was written by Sunkara Satyanarayana and:
q.x: Maa Bhoomi was jointly written by Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao.

q.s: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878, called the 'Gagging Act', was repealed by:
q.x: Lytton passed the Act in 1878; Ripon repealed it in 1882.

q.s: Who was the first Telugu editor in the Madras Presidency to be imprisoned during the Vandemataram movement?
q.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was the first Telugu editor jailed in the movement.

q.s: The first president of the Andhra Desa Library Association (1914) was:
q.x: Mocherla Ramachandra Rao was its first president; Ayyanki and Nalam Krishnarao were secretaries.

q.s: Grandhalaya Sarvasvam (1915), the journal of the Andhra Desa Library Association, was a Telugu:
q.x: Grandhalaya Sarvasvam was a quarterly, revived in 1948 as Andhra Granthalayam.

q.s: The first Andhra library conference of April 1913 was held at:
q.x: It met at Vijayawada on 10 April 1913 with about 200 delegates.

q.s: Who presided over the first Andhra library conference (1913)?
q.x: Chilakamarti presided and said knowledge, like air, should be free to all.

q.s: The Fourth Buddhist Council under Kanishka was held at Kundalavana in:
q.x: The Fourth Council met at Kundalavana (Harwan), Kashmir, and used Sanskrit.

q.s: The Mahavibhasha was compiled at the Fourth Buddhist Council by:
q.x: Vasumitra presided and compiled the Mahavibhasha; Moggaliputta Tissa presided over the Third Council.

q.s: In 1296 Alauddin Khalji, then governor of Kara, raided Devagiri and defeated the Yadava king:
q.x: The 1296 raid on Ramachandra was the first Muslim invasion of the South; Ramachandra submitted again to Malik Kafur in 1307-08.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Yadavas of Devagiri is correct?
o: The 1296 raid on Devagiri was the first Muslim invasion of the South.
After 1296 the Yadavas promised the yearly revenue of Warangal.
Harapaladeva submitted to Malik Kafur in 1307-08.
The Dnyaneshwari was written in the reign of Singhana II.
q.x: The Yadavas promised the revenue of Ellichpur; Ramachandra submitted in 1307-08, in whose reign the Dnyaneshwari (1290) was written.

q.s: Muhammad Ghori's first invasion of India (1175) was directed against:
q.x: Ghori entered by the Gomal Pass and attacked Multan first in 1175.

q.s: In 1186 Muhammad Ghori took Lahore from the last Ghaznavid ruler:
q.x: Khusru Malik, the last Ghaznavid, lost Punjab and Lahore to Ghori in 1186.

q.s: The concept of 'McDonaldisation of society' was developed by:
q.x: Ritzer coined McDonaldisation; Castells gave 'space of flows' and Giddens 'runaway world'.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: 'Runaway world' is Anthony Giddens' phrase; Wallerstein is known for world-systems theory.

q.s: The upward movement of Little-Tradition elements into the Great Tradition is called:
q.x: Universalisation is the upward movement; parochialisation is the downward spread of Great-Tradition elements.

q.s: 'Cultural lag' refers to:
o: Non-material culture lagging behind material change
Material culture lagging behind non-material change
q.x: Cultural lag is the gap when non-material culture fails to keep pace with material change.

q.s: The Indological approach studies Indian society mainly through:
o: Ancient texts such as the Smritis and Puranas
q.x: The Indological (book-view) approach relies on texts; the field-view approach uses contemporary surveys.

q.s: A residence pattern in which a married couple sets up a new home of its own is called:
q.x: Neolocal means a new home; living with the husband's family is patrilocal.

q.s: Who defined the family by common residence, economic co-operation and reproduction?
q.x: This classic definition is Murdock's.

q.s: Among Indian Muslims, the lowest group, made up of converts from untouchable castes, is called:
q.x: Ashraf are of foreign descent, Ajlaf are artisan converts and Arzal are the lowest.

q.s: Buddhists were brought under the Scheduled Castes Order in:
q.x: The SC Order was extended to Sikhs in 1956 and to Buddhists in 1990.

q.s: Longpi pottery of Manipur is associated with which community?
q.x: Longpi black-stone pottery is a Tangkhul Naga craft.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Hui - Sunni Muslim minority of Rakhine State
Rohingya - Sunni Muslim minority of Rakhine State
q.x: The Hui are China's largest Muslim group.

q.s: Which law provides for a civil marriage irrespective of the religion of the parties?
q.x: The Special Marriage Act applies irrespective of religion, even to two persons of the same religion.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh made unmarried daughters coparceners in Hindu joint family property in:
q.x: Andhra Pradesh did this in 1986, well before the national amendment of 2005.

q.s: The form of communalism that uses religion to mobilise votes is called:
q.x: Political communalism uses religion for votes; competition for jobs and resources produces economic communalism.

q.s: Which of the following statements about communalism is correct?
o: Economic communalism uses religion to win votes.
Political communalism grows out of competition for jobs.
Retaliatory communalism tries to harm members of other communities.
q.x: Retaliatory communalism seeks revenge; competition for jobs breeds economic communalism, and political communalism uses religion for votes.

q.s: In the 1920s, the Shuddhi and Sangathan movements were run by the:
q.x: The Arya Samaj ran Shuddhi and Sangathan; Muslim groups ran Tabligh and Tanzim.

q.s: Caste and religion were recorded in the colonial census from the very first one, held in:
q.x: The census recorded caste and religion from 1872.

q.s: Which judgment (1996) upheld Section 309 IPC, overruling P. Rathinam?
o: Gian Kaur v. State of Punjab
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
Common Cause v. Union of India
Aruna Shanbaug v. Union of India
q.x: Gian Kaur (1996) overruled Rathinam (1994), which had held Section 309 invalid.

q.s: Which Law Commission Report recommended decriminalising attempted suicide?
q.x: The 210th Report recommended repealing Section 309 IPC.

q.s: The AASU-led Assam movement (1979-85) against illegal migrants ended with the:
q.x: The movement ended with the Assam Accord of 15 August 1985.

q.s: The Nav Nirman movement of 1974 forced the resignation of the Chief Minister of:
q.x: Chimanbhai Patel of Gujarat resigned in February 1974.

q.s: The Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) is administered by the Ministry of:
q.x: IGNOAPS, part of NSAP, is run by the Ministry of Rural Development.

q.s: Under IGNOAPS, the Centre's monthly pension for persons aged 60-79 is:
q.x: The Centre pays Rs 200 (60-79 years) and Rs 500 (80+), frozen since 2007.

q.s: The national helpline for senior citizens, Elder Line 14567, is a component of:
q.x: Elder Line is part of the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY).

q.s: The Longitudinal Ageing Study in India (LASI) Wave 1 was conducted by:
q.x: LASI was conducted by IIPS, Mumbai, covering persons aged 45+ and their spouses.

q.s: The SACRED portal of the Government of India is meant for:
o: Free assistive devices for the elderly
q.x: SACRED connects senior citizens with job opportunities; SAGE supports elder-care start-ups.

q.s: The Vibrant Villages Programme is implemented by the Ministry of:
q.x: The Vibrant Villages Programme for border villages is under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

q.s: SEED (2022), a scheme for Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes, is run by the Ministry of:
q.x: SEED is a scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

q.s: The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) was launched in:
q.x: PMGKAY began in 2020 under the PM Garib Kalyan Package as COVID-19 relief.

q.s: Which of the following statements about PMGKAY is correct?
o: It provides free foodgrains to NFSA beneficiaries.
It was created by the NFSA, 2013 itself.
q.x: PMGKAY (2020) gives free grain to all NFSA beneficiaries.

q.s: Under PMFBY, the farmer's premium for kharif crops is:
q.x: Premiums are 2% for kharif, 1.5% for rabi and 5% for commercial and horticultural crops.

q.s: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (2016) replaced:
q.x: PMFBY replaced the National Agricultural Insurance Scheme and the Modified NAIS.

q.s: ALIMCO, which makes assistive devices for persons with disabilities, is under the Ministry of:
q.x: ALIMCO (1972) is under the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities.

q.s: The Central Rehabilitation Register is maintained by the:
o: Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
q.x: The RCI maintains the Central Rehabilitation Register.

q.s: The Rooppur project in Bangladesh, built with Russian help, is a:
q.x: Rooppur is a Russia-built nuclear plant.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Maitree at Rampal is a thermal power plant, not a hydro project.

q.s: The first India-Africa Forum Summit was held in 2008 at:
q.x: IAFS-I was in New Delhi (2008) and IAFS-II in Addis Ababa (2011).

q.s: The second India-Africa Forum Summit (2011) was held at:
q.x: IAFS-II was held at Addis Ababa.

q.s: Who became the Director-General of UNESCO on 15 November 2025?
q.x: Khaled El-Enany of Egypt became UNESCO's first Arab Director-General.

q.s: How many Member States did UNESCO have in 2025-26?
q.x: UNESCO had 194 Member States.

q.s: The New Development Bank set up by the BRICS countries is headquartered at:
q.x: The NDB is headquartered at Shanghai; its founders have equal votes and no veto.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the New Development Bank is correct?
o: Its founding members hold equal votes and no one has a veto.
Its membership is restricted to BRICS countries.
It is headquartered at New Delhi.
China holds a veto over its decisions.
q.x: NDB founders have equal votes; it is at Shanghai and open to all UN members.

q.s: Which World Bank Group institution provides political-risk insurance and guarantees?
q.x: MIGA gives political-risk insurance; IFC finances the private sector.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: IFC finances the private sector; ICSID settles investment disputes.

q.s: The Mekong Ganga Cooperation was launched in November 2000 at:
q.x: MGC was launched at Vientiane, Laos.

q.s: How many member countries does the Mekong Ganga Cooperation have?
q.x: India, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam are the six members.

q.s: The G20 Summit of 2025, the first held in Africa, took place at:
q.x: South Africa hosted the 2025 G20 Summit at Johannesburg.

q.s: Which of the following G20 Summit year - venue pairs is NOT correct?
q.x: The 2024 summit was at Rio de Janeiro; Johannesburg hosted it in 2025.

q.s: Which country has the largest NRI population, about 3.5 million?
q.x: The UAE hosts the largest NRI population; India is the world's top remittance recipient.

q.s: The AP Non-Resident Telugu Society (APNRTS) was set up in May 2016 by:
o: the Ministry of Overseas Indian Affairs
q.x: APNRTS is an AP Government body chaired by the Chief Minister.

q.s: The English handwritten original of the Constitution of India was calligraphed by:
q.x: Raizada wrote the English original; Vasant Krishan Vaidya wrote the Hindi original.

q.s: The Hindi handwritten original of the Constitution was calligraphed by:
q.x: Vasant Krishan Vaidya calligraphed the Hindi copy.

q.s: How many members did the Board of Control set up by Pitt's India Act, 1784 have?
q.x: The Board of Control had six members; the Act also reduced the Governor-General's council to three.

q.s: The power given by the Act of 1786 to override the Council was first used by:
q.x: The 1786 Act was passed so that Cornwallis could override his Council and act as Commander-in-Chief.

q.s: Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
q.x: Mountbatten was the first; Rajagopalachari was the last and only Indian Governor-General.

q.s: Until the first Lok Sabha met in 1952, the functions of Parliament were performed by:
o: the Constituent Assembly as Provisional Parliament
q.x: After 26 January 1950 the Constituent Assembly acted as the Provisional Parliament.

q.s: How many members of the Constituent Assembly signed the Constitution on 24 January 1950?
q.x: 284 members signed it; the Assembly then had 299 members.

q.s: The Constituent Assembly held how many sessions?
q.x: It held 11 sessions over 165 days.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the original Constitution of 1950 is correct?
o: It had a Preamble, 395 Articles, 25 Parts and 12 Schedules.
It had a Preamble, 470 Articles, 25 Parts and 8 Schedules.
It had a Preamble, 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.
It had a Preamble, 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 12 Schedules.
q.x: The original had 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules; the Schedules have since grown to 12.

q.s: In the Interim Government of 1946, Jagjivan Ram held the portfolio of:
q.x: Jagjivan Ram held Labour; C.H. Bhabha held Works, Mines and Power.

q.s: Which of the following Interim Government (1946) member - portfolio pairs is NOT correct?
q.x: C.H. Bhabha held Works, Mines and Power; Rajendra Prasad held Food and Agriculture.

q.s: In November 1947, Hyderabad signed with India a:
q.x: Hyderabad signed only a Standstill Agreement; it acceded after Operation Polo (1948).

q.s: Under the Instrument of Accession, a princely State ceded to India:
q.x: Accession covered only defence, external affairs and communications.

q.s: The Citizenship (Amendment) Rules under the CAA, 2019 became effective on:
q.x: The CAA Rules were notified effective 11 March 2024.

q.s: Under the CAA, 2019 the residence requirement for naturalisation of the covered communities was reduced to:
q.x: It was cut from eleven to five years, not removed.

q.s: The emergency provisions are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
q.x: Articles 352-360 form Part XVIII.

q.s: The suspension of Fundamental Rights during an Emergency is borrowed from the Constitution of:
q.x: It comes from the Weimar Constitution; the emergency scheme itself is from the GoI Act, 1935.

q.s: Which Amendment added 'public order' as a ground of restriction under Article 19(2) after the Romesh Thappar case?
q.x: The ban on Cross Roads was struck down because public order was not then a ground; the 1st Amendment added it.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Romesh Thappar v. State of Madras (1950) is correct?
o: 'Public order' was then already a ground under Article 19(2).
The ban on Cross Roads was upheld.
It led to the Forty-second Amendment.
The ban on the journal Cross Roads was struck down.
q.x: The ban fell because public order was not yet a 19(2) ground; the First Amendment added it.

q.s: The expression 'procedure established by law' in Article 21 is taken from the Constitution of:
q.x: Article 21 follows Japan; 'due process of law' is an American concept.

q.s: Which case upheld the death penalty in the 'rarest of rare' cases?
o: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab
A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
Kharak Singh v. State of U.P.
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
q.x: Bachan Singh (1980) held that capital punishment does not violate Article 21.

q.s: Which judgment held that a proclamation under Article 356 is subject to judicial review and that majority must be tested on the floor of the House?
q.x: The nine-judge Bommai bench laid down both principles.

q.s: In Rameshwar Prasad (2006), the Supreme Court declared void the dissolution of the Legislative Assembly of:
q.x: The case concerned the 2005 dissolution of the Bihar Assembly.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment provided 10 per cent reservation for the Economically Weaker Sections?
q.x: The 103rd Amendment (2019) added Articles 15(6) and 16(6).

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: 76th Amendment - Tamil Nadu's reservation law in the Ninth Schedule
105th Amendment - States' power to identify SEBCs
77th Amendment - Reservation in promotion for SCs/STs
q.x: The 85th Amendment gave consequential seniority; EWS reservation came by the 103rd.

q.s: Impeachment of the President of India requires a resolution passed by:
o: A simple majority of members present and voting
Two-thirds of members present and voting in the Lok Sabha only
Two-thirds of the total membership of each House
An effective majority of each House
q.x: Impeachment needs two-thirds of the total membership, the strictest majority.

q.s: A resolution under Article 249 empowering Parliament to legislate on a State List subject must be passed by:
o: The Lok Sabha by two-thirds of total membership
Both Houses by a simple majority
The Rajya Sabha by two-thirds of members present and voting
q.x: Article 249 needs a two-thirds present-and-voting resolution of the Rajya Sabha.

q.s: In which case (1967) did the Supreme Court hold that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights?
q.x: Golaknath (1967) reversed Shankari Prasad (1951); Kesavananda (1973) gave the basic structure doctrine.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment (1971) was enacted to nullify the Golaknath judgment?
q.x: The 24th Amendment affirmed Parliament's power to amend any part, including Fundamental Rights.

q.s: Which of the following Bills lapses on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha?
o: A Bill returned by the President for reconsideration
A Bill passed by both Houses and pending the President's assent
A Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha but not passed by the Lok Sabha
A Bill passed by the Lok Sabha but pending in the Rajya Sabha
q.x: A Bill passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha lapses; the others survive.

q.s: Within how many days must the Rajya Sabha return a Money Bill with its recommendations?
q.x: The Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend a Money Bill; it can only recommend within 14 days.

q.s: For which of the following Bills is there no provision for a joint sitting of the two Houses?
q.x: If the Houses disagree on an Amendment Bill it simply fails.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly?
q.x: Art. 168 - constitution of State Legislatures; Art. 175 - Governor's address; Art. 178 - Speaker; Art. 211 - bar on discussing a judge's conduct.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 211 - No discussion of a High Court judge's conduct
q.x: Article 175 is the Governor's right of address and messages.

q.s: How many members of the 58-member Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council are nominated by the Governor?
q.x: 20 are elected by local authorities, 20 by MLAs, 5 by graduates, 5 by teachers and 8 are nominated.

q.s: Which of the following does NOT form an electorate for the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council?
q.x: Only teachers of secondary schools and above elect the teachers' members.

q.s: Disputes relating to the election of the President of India are decided by:
q.x: Only the Supreme Court decides such disputes; acts done before the election is voided remain valid.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the election of the President is correct?
o: Election disputes are decided by the Election Commission.
His election can be challenged because of vacancies in the electoral college.
Acts done by him before his election is declared void remain valid.
Election disputes are decided by the Delhi High Court.
q.x: Earlier acts stay valid, vacancies are no ground, and only the Supreme Court decides disputes.

q.s: Which of the following can an ordinance issued under Article 123 NOT do?
o: Be promulgated when Parliament is not in session
Be withdrawn by the President at any time
Have the same force as an Act of Parliament
q.x: Amendment needs Article 368; an ordinance is not an exercise of constituent power.

q.s: The collegium system for appointment of judges is based on:
q.x: The collegium is not in the Constitution or any Act; it derives from the Judges Cases.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the collegium system is correct?
o: The collegium is provided for in Article 124.
If the collegium reiterates a name returned by the Government, the Government is bound to appoint the person.
Judges are formally appointed by the Chief Justice of India.
High Court appointments are initiated by the Chief Justice of India alone.
q.x: Reiteration binds the Government; the President appoints under Articles 124(2) and 217(1), and the collegium is not in the Constitution.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Article 371D, providing for an Andhra Pradesh Administrative Tribunal?
q.x: The 32nd Amendment (1973) inserted Art. 371D; APAT was constituted by a Presidential order under 371D(3).

q.s: A State Administrative Tribunal under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 is set up by:
o: The Central Government at the request of the State
The State Government under a State law
The High Court of the State
q.x: The Centre sets up SATs on a State's request; a joint tribunal can serve two or more States.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Administrative Tribunal was abolished in:
q.x: APAT started on 6 July 1976, Telangana was removed in 2016 and APAT was abolished in 2020.

q.s: After APAT was abolished, its service cases were transferred to the:
q.x: Its pending cases went to the AP High Court.

q.s: Appeals against orders of SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA are heard by the:
q.x: SAT hears SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA appeals; APTEL hears appeals from electricity regulators.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: TDSAT hears appeals from TRAI and IT Act officers; SEBI appeals go to SAT.

q.s: Which of the following subjects is NOT in the State List?
q.x: Broadcasting is a Union subject; the other three are State subjects.

q.s: 'Water' (Entry 17) is placed in which list of the Seventh Schedule?
o: None; it is a residuary subject
q.x: Water is in the State List, subject to Entry 56 of the Union List on inter-State rivers.

q.s: The doctrine of 'pith and substance' is associated with which case?
o: State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara (1951)
K.C. Gajapati Narayan Deo v. State of Orissa (1953)
Bhikaji Narain Dhakras v. State of M.P. (1955)
q.x: Balsara - pith and substance; Gajapati Narayan Deo - colourable legislation; Bhikaji - eclipse.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Colourable legislation is linked with K.C. Gajapati Narayan Deo (1953).

q.s: Under Article 77, all executive action of the Government of India is taken in the name of the:
q.x: Executive action is expressed in the name of the President.

q.s: Which Article provides that Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses?
q.x: Under Article 79 the President is a part of Parliament.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's share in the States' divisible pool under the 16th Finance Commission is:
q.x: AP's share was 4.305% (14th FC), 4.047% (15th FC) and 4.217% (16th FC).

q.s: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office:
o: By the President on the advice of the Prime Minister
By a simple majority resolution of the Lok Sabha
In like manner and on like grounds as a Supreme Court judge
By the President on the recommendation of the CJI
q.x: The CEC has the same removal protection as an SC judge; Election Commissioners are removed on the CEC's recommendation.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: State Election Commissioner - Removed like a High Court judge
Election Commissioner - Removed on the CEC's recommendation
Chief Electoral Officer of a State - Removed like a High Court judge
Chief Election Commissioner - Removed like a Supreme Court judge
q.x: The Chief Electoral Officer of a State is removed by the ECI.

q.s: Posts may be excluded from consultation with the UPSC by regulations made by:
q.x: The President makes such regulations, which must be laid before Parliament for at least 14 days.

q.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes submits its annual reports to the:
q.x: The NCSC reports to the President, who lays the reports before Parliament.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the National Commission for Scheduled Castes is correct?
o: It submits its reports to the Prime Minister.
It can punish those it finds guilty.
While investigating, it has the powers of a civil court trying a suit.
q.x: It has civil-court powers but cannot punish; it reports to the President and functions under Article 338.

q.s: Under Section 8(3) of the RTI Act, 2005, most exemptions lapse after:
q.x: Most exemptions cease after 20 years; information that cannot be denied to Parliament cannot be denied to any person.

q.s: The Central Bureau of Investigation was added to the Second Schedule of the RTI Act in:
q.x: The CBI was brought under Section 24 in 2011.

q.s: Organisations in the Second Schedule of the RTI Act must still disclose information relating to:
q.x: The proviso to Section 24 keeps corruption and human-rights information open.

q.s: Which State was the first to pass a Lokayukta law, in 1970?
q.x: Odisha's law came in 1970 though its institution started only in 1983.

q.s: Karnataka's Lokayukta, with its own police wing, was set up under:
q.x: It was set up under the State's own Karnataka Lokayukta Act, 1984.

q.s: The Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards were set up under:
o: The Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956
q.x: KRMB and GRMB were created under the APRA, 2014.

q.s: How much Krishna water had KWDT-I allotted to undivided Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: KWDT-I allotted 811 tmcft; the ad hoc split since 2014-15 is 512 (AP) to 299 (Telangana).

q.s: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution (1973) demanding greater State autonomy was adopted by the:
q.x: It was the Akali Dal's resolution; the CPI(M) memorandum of West Bengal came in 1977.

q.s: Under which Article did Kerala file its suit against the Centre's Net Borrowing Ceiling in 2024?
q.x: Article 131 gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction in Centre-State disputes.

q.s: Which of the following statements about State of Kerala v. Union of India (2024) is correct?
o: The Net Borrowing Ceiling excludes off-budget borrowings.
Kerala filed the suit under Article 131.
The case was filed in the Kerala High Court.
Kerala filed a writ petition under Article 32.
q.x: The Article 131 suit challenged the ceiling, which counts off-budget borrowings.

q.s: The Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State relations submitted its report in:
q.x: Set up in 1983, it reported in 1988 with 247 recommendations.

q.s: Which of the following was a member of the Sarkaria Commission?
q.x: Its members were B. Sivaraman and S.R. Sen; Punchhi headed the 2007 commission.

q.s: The 'localised emergency' proposed by the Punchhi Commission would let the Centre take over:
o: A district or part of a district for a limited period
An entire State for one year
The State Legislature for six months
All police stations of a State
q.x: Punchhi proposed localised emergency and wanted Article 356 used only as a last resort.

q.s: The Electoral Bond Scheme was notified on:
q.x: It came through the Finance Act, 2017 and was notified on 2 January 2018.

q.s: To encash electoral bonds, a registered party had to have secured at least what share of votes in the last election?
q.x: Only Section 29A parties with at least 1% of the votes could encash them.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the Gram Sabha?
q.x: Art. 243A: the Gram Sabha exercises powers given by State law.

q.s: Gram Panchayat Development Plans are prepared through Gram Sabhas under the People's Plan Campaign called:
q.x: The campaign runs every year from 2 October.

q.s: How many subjects are listed in the Eleventh Schedule for Panchayats?
q.x: Devolution of the 29 subjects is left to the States, hence the unevenness.

q.s: Under the 73rd Amendment, the State Finance Commission is constituted under:
q.x: Article 243I makes the SFC mandatory every five years; its recommendations are advisory.

q.s: Who was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India?
q.x: Fathima Beevi became an SC judge in 1989; Leila Seth was the first woman judge of the Delhi HC.

q.s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Women?
q.x: Jayanti Patnaik was the first NCW chairperson (1992).

q.s: Which of the following is listed in the Twelfth Schedule (Municipalities)?
q.x: Urban poverty alleviation is a Twelfth Schedule subject; the others are Eleventh Schedule subjects.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a market failure?
q.x: Public goods, externalities, monopoly and information asymmetry are market failures that justified an active State.

q.s: Which committee (1993) recommended disinvestment of up to 49% in PSUs reserved for the public sector?
q.x: Rangarajan (1993) - 49%; Ramakrishna (1996) - strategic sale; Kelkar (2015) - PPP review.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Disinvestment Commission (1996) - Roadmap for strategic sale
C. Rangarajan Committee (1993) - Disinvestment up to 49 per cent
Vijay Kelkar Committee (2015) - Review of the PPP model
Vijay Kelkar Committee (2012) - Roadmap for strategic sale
q.x: Kelkar (2012) recommended faster disinvestment.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the six principles of the Citizens' Charter?
q.x: The six principles are quality, choice, standards, value, accountability and transparency.

q.s: In December 2023 PNGRB terminated the authorisation of the Kakinada-Srikakulam gas pipeline after it was surrendered by:
q.x: The pipeline was authorised to APGDC in 2014; APGDC surrendered it.

q.s: Galeru-Nagari irrigation project in Andhra Pradesh is based on the waters of the:
q.x: Galeru-Nagari is a Krishna-based project.

q.s: Which irrigation project of Andhra Pradesh is a National Project under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
q.x: Polavaram was declared a National Project by the APRA, 2014.

q.s: The water-use efficiency of drip irrigation is about:
q.x: Drip is about 90% efficient, far above flood irrigation (30-50%).

q.s: Which of the following statements about irrigation efficiency is correct?
o: Flood irrigation is about 90 per cent efficient.
Basin irrigation is more efficient than drip irrigation.
Drip irrigation is about 30-50 per cent efficient.
Drip irrigation is far more water-efficient than flood irrigation.
q.x: Drip is about 90% efficient; flood or basin irrigation about 30-50%.

q.s: Ports in Andhra Pradesh are managed by the:
q.x: The AP Maritime Board handles the State's ports.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's coastline is about how long?
q.x: AP's coastline is about 1,053 km, the third longest among States.

q.s: According to the NITI Aayog MPI 2023, which Andhra Pradesh district had the lowest multidimensional poverty headcount?
q.x: West Godavari - 2.42% (lowest); Guntur 4.36%; Krishna 4.38%; Chittoor 5.66%.

q.s: The gap between the HDI and the IHDI represents:
o: Loss in human development due to inequality
q.x: IHDI discounts HDI for inequality; the difference is the loss from inequality.

q.s: Which UNDP index adjusts the HDI for planetary pressures and so captures intergenerational inequality?
q.x: The IHDI is intragenerational; the PHDI is intergenerational.

q.s: India's child sex ratio (0-6 years) in Census 2011 was:
q.x: The child sex ratio fell continuously from 976 (1961) to 919 (2011); 943 is the overall sex ratio.

q.s: The 'Laws of Migration' (1885) were formulated by:
q.x: Ravenstein gave the Laws of Migration; Lee gave push-pull with intervening obstacles (1966).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a theory of migration?
q.x: Demographic transition (Notestein) is a population theory; the others are migration models of Ravenstein, Lee and Todaro.

q.s: The Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (2011) provides:
o: A TFR target of 2.1 in high-fertility States
Free, cashless delivery including caesarean in public facilities
Conditional cash for the first live birth
A cash incentive for institutional delivery
q.x: JSSK gives free cashless delivery; JSY (2005) gives cash for institutional delivery.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: PM Matru Vandana Yojana - DBT for the first live birth
JSSK - Free cashless delivery in public facilities
Janani Suraksha Yojana - Cash incentive for institutional delivery
Mission Parivar Vikas - Free cashless delivery in public facilities
q.x: Mission Parivar Vikas aims at TFR 2.1 in seven high-fertility States.

q.s: At the time of Independence (1950-51), agriculture's share in India's national income was about:
q.x: Agriculture was 56.5% in 1950-51; it fell to about 17% by 2017-18.

q.s: The new national accounts series uses which tool to reduce the discrepancy between production and expenditure estimates?
q.x: The 2022-23 series uses Supply and Use Tables to reconcile the two sides.

q.s: The base year of India's new national accounts series is:
q.x: The new series has 2022-23 as base year, replacing 2011-12.

q.s: The GSDP of Andhra Pradesh is compiled by:
o: The State Directorate of Economics and Statistics
q.x: State income is compiled by the State DES.

q.s: GSDP at market prices is obtained from GVA at basic prices by:
o: Adding net factor income from abroad
Adding product taxes and subtracting product subsidies
Adding production taxes and subtracting production subsidies
q.x: Product taxes less subsidies take basic prices to market prices.

q.s: Which of the following does NOT belong to the tertiary sector?
q.x: Research and knowledge services are quaternary; hotels, trade and banking are tertiary.

q.s: The Consumer Pyramids Household Survey of employment is conducted by:
q.x: CMIE runs the private monthly CPHS.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Labour Bureau - Consumer Pyramids Household Survey
q.x: The Labour Bureau runs the EUS and Quarterly Employment Survey; CPHS is CMIE's.

q.s: About what share of India's workers are informally employed?
q.x: Nearly 90% of workers are informally employed; informal employment exists even in the formal sector.

q.s: The Aspirational Blocks Programme launched in January 2023 covers how many blocks?
q.x: It covers 500 blocks; 112 is the number of Aspirational Districts.

q.s: VB-G RAM G, which replaced MGNREGA, guarantees how many days of wage employment a year?
q.x: VB-G RAM G raised the guarantee from 100 to 125 days.

q.s: Simon Kuznets' original inverted-U curve related per capita income to:
q.x: Kuznets' curve was about inequality; its environmental version was shown by Grossman and Krueger (1991).

q.s: Which Finance Commission did away with the distinction between general and Special Category States?
q.x: The 14th FC also ended the Plan/non-Plan distinction and gave no sector-specific grants.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Fourteenth Finance Commission is correct?
o: It ended the Plan/non-Plan distinction in assessing States' needs.
It retained the distinction between general and Special Category States.
It gave grants only to urban local bodies.
q.x: It took the entire revenue expenditure into account, gave no sector grants and gave most local-body money to gram panchayats.

q.s: Under which Article does tax devolution from the Union to the States take place?
q.x: Art. 270 governs sharing of taxes; Art. 275 provides grants-in-aid.

q.s: Special Category Status for States was introduced in:
q.x: SCS began in 1969, usually credited to the 5th Finance Commission; it has no constitutional provision.

q.s: The Gadgil Formula, which reserved a share of Normal Central Assistance for Special Category States, was approved by the:
q.x: The NDC approved the Gadgil Formula; the Gadgil-Mukherjee Formula followed in 1991.

q.s: Which of the following statements about NITI Aayog is correct?
o: It was set up by an Act of Parliament.
Its CEO is ex officio its Vice-Chairperson.
Its Vice-Chairperson and its CEO are separate posts.
Its Chairperson is the Union Finance Minister.
q.x: NITI Aayog (2015) was set up by executive resolution, is chaired by the PM and has a separate Vice-Chairperson and CEO.

q.s: Consent-based sharing of a person's financial data in India takes place through:
q.x: RBI-regulated NBFC-Account Aggregators enable consent-based data sharing.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: ONDC - Open network for digital commerce
OCEN - Person- and purpose-specific prepaid voucher
e-RUPI - Person- and purpose-specific prepaid voucher
Account Aggregator - Consent-based sharing of financial data
q.x: OCEN is a credit protocol linking lenders and marketplaces; e-RUPI is the voucher.

q.s: Who was the first Indian Governor of the Reserve Bank of India?
q.x: C.D. Deshmukh was Governor in 1943-49.

q.s: Who was the RBI Governor during 1982-85?
q.x: Manmohan Singh was Governor in 1982-85; Rangarajan 1992-97; Jalan 1997-2003.

q.s: In its role as 'controller of credit', the RBI:
o: Controls money and credit through monetary policy
Manages the public debt of the Government
q.x: As controller of credit the RBI runs monetary policy; public debt is part of its banker-to-Government role.

q.s: In which role does the RBI provide emergency liquidity to banks when no one else will?
q.x: As lender of last resort the RBI supplies emergency liquidity to banks.

q.s: Which of the following is a qualitative (selective) instrument of monetary control?
q.x: Margin requirements and moral suasion are qualitative; repo, OMO, CRR and SLR are quantitative.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a quantitative instrument of credit control?
q.x: Moral suasion is a qualitative (selective) tool.

q.s: Between 1998 and 2014 the RBI's monetary policy followed which framework?
q.x: The multiple indicator approach was used before flexible inflation targeting; it was criticised as opaque.

q.s: From 1 April 2027 the RBI moves bank provisioning to which model?
q.x: The RBI shifts from the incurred-loss model to a forward-looking three-stage ECL model.

q.s: Under the RBI's Expected Credit Loss model, Stage 2 assets require:
q.x: Stage 1 needs 12-month provisioning; Stage 2 needs lifetime expected-loss provisioning.

q.s: Which is the largest subsidy in the Union Budget 2026-27?
q.x: Food subsidy (Rs 2,27,629 crore) is the largest; food and fertiliser together are 87% of the bill.

q.s: Budget 2026-27 set the Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) at:
q.x: Budget 2026-27 set MAT at 14%, with no new MAT credit after 1 April 2026.

q.s: The Minimum Alternate Tax was first introduced in the Budget of:
q.x: MAT came in 1987-88 (Section 115J), was withdrawn in 1990 and returned in 1996-97.

q.s: Which of the following is excluded from GST by the Constitution itself under Article 366(12A)?
q.x: The five petroleum products are within GST but not yet levied; only alcoholic liquor is constitutionally excluded.

q.s: In Mohit Minerals (2022), the Supreme Court held that the recommendations of the GST Council are:
o: Binding on Parliament and State Legislatures
q.x: The Court called the Council's recommendations persuasive.

q.s: What is the weight of the Centre's vote in the GST Council?
q.x: The Centre has one-third and the States two-thirds of the weight; decisions need three-fourths.

q.s: India's largest import item is:
q.x: Crude petroleum is the largest; with gold and petroleum products it makes up about a third of imports.

q.s: Under the 'Districts as Export Hubs' initiative, each district export plan prioritises:
q.x: Each district plan prioritises 2-3 products or services.

q.s: An official reduction in the value of a currency under a fixed exchange rate regime is called:
q.x: Devaluation/revaluation are official changes under a fixed regime; depreciation/appreciation are market-driven.

q.s: What was India's rank in the Global Hunger Index 2025?
q.x: India ranked 102nd of 123 with a score of 25.8 ('serious').

q.s: The Global Hunger Index is published by:
q.x: The GHI is published by Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe; the FAO leads the SOFI report.

q.s: Under the NFSA, 2013, an Antyodaya Anna Yojana household is entitled to:
q.x: AAY households get a flat 35 kg; the 2026 draft Bill proposes 7 kg per person capped at 35 kg.

q.s: HYV crops of the Green Revolution resist lodging because they are:
q.x: HYV seeds were dwarf varieties used with fertiliser and water; quick maturity allowed double cropping.

q.s: The benefits of the Green Revolution remained confined mainly to:
o: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
q.x: Its gains came mainly in areas with assured irrigation.

q.s: Agricultural markets in Andhra Pradesh are governed by the:
o: AP (Agricultural Produce and Livestock) Markets Act, 1966
q.x: The 1966 State Act governs markets; agricultural markets are a State subject.

q.s: The first step in setting up a regulated agricultural market is:
q.x: The market area is notified first; the committee and then the yard follow.

q.s: The Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS) is a component of:
q.x: PDPS, with PSS and PPSS, forms PM-AASHA; economists prefer such payments to a legal MSP.

q.s: Under Decentralised Procurement, foodgrains for TPDS are procured, stored and distributed by:
q.x: Under DCP, designated States handle procurement and distribution themselves.

q.s: 'CAP' storage of foodgrains stands for:
q.x: CAP keeps grain on raised plinths under polythene covers.

q.s: What was India's rank in the IMD World Competitiveness Ranking 2025?
q.x: India ranked 41st in the IMD ranking of 2025.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Jan Vishwas 2.0 Bill is correct?
o: It decriminalises all 355 provisions it amends.
q.x: It amends 16 Acts and decriminalises 288 of 355 provisions.

q.s: The India Semiconductor Mission functions under the:
q.x: ISM, approved in 2021, works under the Digital India Corporation of MeitY.

q.s: Most of the projects under ISM 1.0 are located in:
q.x: Most ISM 1.0 projects are in Gujarat.

q.s: PM E-DRIVE, launched in September 2024, replaced which scheme?
q.x: PM E-DRIVE (Rs 10,900 crore) replaced FAME-II.

q.s: PM E-DRIVE is implemented by the Ministry of:
q.x: The Ministry of Heavy Industries runs PM E-DRIVE.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of small and cottage industries?
q.x: They are labour-intensive with low capital per worker and have been a priority since the First Plan.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an external cause of industrial sickness?
q.x: Poor working-capital management is an internal cause.

q.s: In which year was Andhra Pradesh the only State with double-digit GSDP growth (12.16 per cent, the series peak)?
q.x: 2015-16 was the peak; 2020-21 was the low at 1.52%.

q.s: Under Section 90(4) of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Polavaram project is to be executed by:
q.x: Section 90(4) gives execution and clearances to the Centre; NITI Aayog (2016) suggested AP execute it with central funding.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Section 90 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 is correct?
o: Under Section 90(3), the consent of Telangana is deemed to have been given.
Under Section 90(4), the AP Government obtains all clearances.
Section 90(3) requires the express consent of Telangana.
Section 90 deals with the Apex Council on river waters.
q.x: Telangana's consent is deemed; the Centre executes Polavaram and obtains clearances under 90(4).

q.s: Under PMMSY, the subsidy for women, SC and ST beneficiaries is:
q.x: General category gets 40% (24% GoI + 16% GoAP); women/SC/ST get 60% (36% + 24%).

q.s: Which State ranked first in India in micro-irrigation in 2024-25?
q.x: AP ranked first nationally in micro-irrigation in 2024-25.

q.s: The Rs 10,000 crore Micro Irrigation Fund is maintained through:
q.x: The Micro Irrigation Fund is operated through NABARD.

q.s: The AP Single Desk Portal gives pre-establishment and pre-operation approvals within:
q.x: Approvals are given within 21 days; investors need not visit regulators.

q.s: Jawaharlal Nehru Pharma City in Andhra Pradesh is located at:
q.x: JN Pharma City is at Parawada (Visakhapatnam); the central SEZ is at Duvvada.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: EMC-1 is at Renigunta (Tirupati).

q.s: The Orvakal industrial node in Kurnool district is part of which corridor?
q.x: Orvakal is a node of the Hyderabad-Bengaluru corridor; NICDIT funds its trunk infrastructure.

q.s: Visakhapatnam port is a natural harbour sheltered by which headland?
q.x: The Dolphin's Nose headland shelters the Visakhapatnam harbour.

q.s: Google's 1 GW AI data centre in Andhra Pradesh is coming up near:
q.x: The Google AI hub is at Tarluvada, Visakhapatnam.

q.s: Google's AI hub at Visakhapatnam is being built with:
q.x: Its partners are AdaniConneX and Airtel; the foundation stone was laid on 28 April 2026.

q.s: The hub of Andhra Pradesh's Ratan Tata Innovation Hub is at:
q.x: The hub is at Amaravati (Mangalagiri).

q.s: The vision of the Ratan Tata Innovation Hub is:
q.x: Its stated vision is 'One Family, One Entrepreneur'.

q.s: The National Green Hydrogen Mission targets annual green hydrogen production by 2030 of:
q.x: The Mission (2023) targets 5 MMT a year by 2030.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Non-fossil capacity above 40 per cent - First NDC, by 2030
500 GW non-fossil capacity - COP26 Panchamrit, by 2030
175 GW renewable energy - COP26 Panchamrit, by 2030
5 MMT green hydrogen a year - National Green Hydrogen Mission, by 2030
q.x: 175 GW was India's renewable target for 2022.

q.s: The Principal Bench of the National Green Tribunal is at:
q.x: The Principal Bench is at Delhi; Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai have zonal benches.

q.s: The National Green Tribunal (2010) replaced the:
q.x: The NGT Act, 2010 replaced the NEAA.

q.s: The report 'Our Common Future' (1987) was prepared by the:
o: World Commission on Environment and Development
q.x: The Brundtland Commission (WCED) wrote Our Common Future and defined sustainable development.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: World Conservation Strategy - Club of Rome
The Limits to Growth - Club of Rome
q.x: The World Conservation Strategy (1980) was by IUCN, UNEP and WWF.

q.s: The Earth's magnetic field is generated in the:
q.x: Convection in the liquid outer core generates the field.

q.s: The Earth's hydrosphere was formed mainly by:
o: Condensation of degassed water vapour falling as rain
Capture of water from the solar wind
q.x: Degassing released water vapour, which condensed and fell as rain.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's area is about what share of India's total area?
q.x: AP covers about 4.96% of India's area.

q.s: In terms of area, Andhra Pradesh is India's:
q.x: After 2014, AP is the seventh largest State; the 82°30'E IST meridian passes through it.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an intrusive igneous rock?
q.x: Basalt is extrusive, formed by quick cooling of lava.

q.s: Lines joining places where an earthquake shock arrives at the same time are called:
q.x: Homoseismal (coseismal) lines join points of equal arrival time; isoseismal lines join equal intensity.

q.s: A 'seismic doublet' refers to:
o: Two seismic waves of different speed
A main shock followed by aftershocks
Two independent earthquakes of similar magnitude close in time and place
An earthquake followed by a tsunami
q.x: A doublet is two similar, independent quakes, as at Caracas in June 2026.

q.s: Which of the following is a shield volcano?
q.x: Mauna Loa is built of fluid basalt; Fuji and Vesuvius are composite and Mount Kenya is extinct.

q.s: Narcondam volcano in the Andaman Sea is classified as:
q.x: Narcondam is dormant; Barren Island is India's active volcano.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of caves in Andhra Pradesh are both karst (limestone) caves?
q.x: Belum and Borra are karstic limestone caves; Undavalli and Bojjannakonda are rock-cut.

q.s: The northward shift of the ITCZ during the northern summer is caused by:
o: The apparent northward movement of the overhead Sun
q.x: The ITCZ follows the overhead Sun; its shift in turn helps the monsoon.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the ITCZ is correct?
o: It shifts northward during the northern summer.
It remains fixed over the equator throughout the year.
It moves north because it helps the monsoon circulation.
It shifts southward during the northern summer.
q.x: The ITCZ follows the overhead Sun northward; its shift helps the monsoon, not the reverse.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Specific humidity is expressed in g/kg.

q.s: An isohyet is a line joining places of equal:
q.x: Isohyet - rainfall; isoneph - cloudiness; isobar - pressure; isogonic - declination.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Isogonic lines join places of equal magnetic declination; isotherms join equal temperature.

q.s: The Siberian High is an example of a:
q.x: It is built by cold, dense cP/cA air and gives clear skies, fog and frost.

q.s: Tropical cyclones of the North-west Pacific, affecting the Philippines and Japan, are called:
q.x: They are typhoons in the NW Pacific; India's storms are called cyclones.

q.s: The highest air temperature on Earth (56.7°C, 1913) was recorded at:
q.x: The WMO rejected Al Aziziya's record; Dasht-e-Lut's 70.7°C is a land-surface reading.

q.s: Which of the following statements about world temperature records is correct?
o: The WMO accepted Al Aziziya's record as the highest.
The WMO rejected the Al Aziziya heat record.
The 56.7°C record was set in the Sahara.
Dasht-e-Lut holds the record for the highest air temperature.
q.x: Death Valley's 56.7°C (1913) stands; Dasht-e-Lut's 70.7°C is a land-surface reading.

q.s: Which region of Andhra Pradesh is semi-arid and most prone to drought?
q.x: Rayalaseema (Anantapur, Kurnool, Kadapa) has low and erratic rainfall.

q.s: In Trewartha's climatic classification of India, 'Am' denotes:
o: Humid sub-tropical climate of the Ganga plain
Tropical monsoon climate of the west coast
q.x: Am is the west-coast tropical monsoon; the Peninsula's savanna is Aw; the Ganga plain is Caw.

q.s: Trewartha's classification of climate is a modification of the scheme of:
q.x: Trewartha modified Koeppen, keeping its temperature-rainfall basis.

q.s: Halons, which deplete ozone, were mainly used in:
q.x: CFCs - refrigeration and aerosols; halons - fire extinguishers; methyl bromide - fumigant.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Methyl bromide is a fumigant; halons are used in fire extinguishers.

q.s: A thermocline or halocline in the ocean:
o: Marks the boundary of the continental shelf
q.x: The sharp density contrast across a cline blocks vertical exchange.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Niti Pass links Uttarakhand with Tibet, not Myanmar.

q.s: The largest kayal (backwater) of the Malabar coast is:
q.x: Vembanad is the largest kayal of Kerala.

q.s: The Buckingham Canal runs along which coast?
q.x: It runs along the Coromandel coast between Kakinada and Parangipettai; the Utkal plain is in Odisha.

q.s: IMD classifies all-India monsoon rainfall as 'normal' when it is:
q.x: Deficient <90%; below normal 90-95%; normal 96-104%; above normal 105-110%; excess >110%.

q.s: Rayalaseema receives comparatively little south-west monsoon rain because it lies:
o: In the path of retreating monsoon cyclones
In the rain shadow of the Western Ghats
On the windward side of the Eastern Ghats
Close to the Bay of Bengal
q.x: It is in the rain shadow of the Western Ghats and the Karnataka-Telangana highlands.

q.s: The Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre is housed at:
q.x: ITEWC at INCOIS has worked 24x7 since 2007.

q.s: INCOIS is an autonomous body under the:
q.x: INCOIS is under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, not ISRO.

q.s: The Tummalapalle uranium mine is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Tummalapalle is in YSR Kadapa district.

q.s: The Jaduguda and Narwapahar uranium mines are in:
q.x: Both are in Jharkhand.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a node of the Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor?
q.x: The six UP nodes are Agra, Aligarh, Lucknow, Kanpur, Jhansi and Chitrakoot.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a node of the Tamil Nadu Defence Industrial Corridor?
q.x: The TN nodes are Chennai, Coimbatore, Hosur, Salem and Tiruchirappalli.
